note: Clean pass with disclosures. (1) SOURCE IS LEVEL 1. The study's own deposit (S1 Data, SPSS .sav, PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0264722.s001, CC BY 4.0) carries a variable label on every HCS_trust column and a value label on every response level; item_text and option_text are those labels verbatim. data/pavic_2022_vaccine_conspiracy.py melts HCS_trust1..HCS_trust8 straight off that .sav, so the IRW item code IS the source column name -- code-derivation pattern 1, no positional inference anywhere, which is why mapping_basis=data_labels and no Step 5b route is owed. (2) ONE DELIBERATE EDIT. Five labels end with the depositors' annotation ' (reversed item)' (HCS_trust2, 4, 5, 7, 8); that is a coding note, not administered wording, and it was stripped. Nothing else was changed -- the typographic apostrophe in ‘patients’ health’ and ‘patients’ needs’ is the .sav's own character. (3) INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE MAPPING. Shea et al. (2008) J Gen Intern Med 23(6):727-732, PMC2517896, Table 3 prints the 9 revised-HCSD items; the paper's Methods says the authors 'left out the item about the equal treatment of patients of all races and ethnicities'. The 8 .sav labels are Shea's items 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 verbatim and in order, with Shea's item 7 (race/ethnicity) absent exactly as stated -- so the labels reproduce a published instrument rather than being a depositor's paraphrase. (4) ENGLISH SHIPPED FOR A CROATIAN ADMINISTRATION. The sample is 577 college- and university-educated people in Croatia recruited by snowball to an online questionnaire, so the administered language was Croatian. The deposit and the paper's only other supplement (S1 Highlights, .docx -- five bullet points, no instrument) contain no Croatian item text: the .sav's labels are entirely English and the sole Croatian string in the file is the derived variable name Spol_pismenost_interakcija. Recoverability is scoped to the deposit and the paper's supplements, so this is the documented fallback: English in the base fields, _translated columns empty, language=Croatian, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (5) NO INSTRUCTIONS PUBLISHED. Neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces an instruction stem; the paper states only that 'all the items were answered on a five-point scale ranging from 1 = completely disagree to 5 = completely agree'. instructions is left blank rather than paraphrased from that sentence, and the anchors it names match the .sav value labels shipped here. (6) RESPONSES ARE RAW. The .sav also carries HCS_trust2_rec/4_rec/5_rec/7_rec/8_rec and HCS_trust_total; the processing script uses only the raw columns, so the five reverse-worded items are stored UNREVERSED in the live table. (7) RIGHTS. No clause to quote, so silence is permission (irw#1945 test: nothing here reserves a fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution right). The instrument is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. IRW's copy came from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit's own variable labels. The originator's side was checked: the only rights statement locatable on the Shea et al. source is the PMC/journal copyright line '© Society of General Internal Medicine 2008', which is a notice about the article and not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case); elsihub.org/research-tool/health-care-system-distrust-scale returned HTTP 403 to a direct fetch and no substitute statement of terms was found on any Penn/Shea page. Absence of a retrievable clause is not absence of a clause, so this basis is recorded rather than asserted as exhaustive.
public_note: Item text for pavic_2022_healthcare_trust is English, but the study was administered in Croatian - 577 college- and university-educated respondents in Croatia - and neither the paper nor its supplements publishes the Croatian wording, so these are not the sentences respondents read. The English is the study's own, taken verbatim from the SPSS variable labels in its CC BY deposit, and matches Shea et al.'s (2008) published revised Health Care System Distrust Scale word for word for all 8 items (Shea's item 7, on equal treatment regardless of race or ethnicity, was omitted by the authors as inapplicable in Croatia). Responses are stored raw: the five reverse-worded items - HCS_trust2, 4, 5, 7, 8 - run opposite to the other three and must be reversed before a trust total is scored.

source_ref: Pavic Z, Suljok A (2022) 'Vaccination conspiracy beliefs among social science & humanities and STEM educated people - An analysis of the mediation paths', PLOS ONE 17(3):e0264722, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0264722 (CC BY 4.0). Processing script data/pavic_2022_vaccine_conspiracy.py. Instrument original: Martin LR, Petrie KJ (2017) Ann Behav Med 51(5):652-660, doi:10.1007/s12160-017-9888-y, Table 2 (PDF cached from https://www.fmhs.auckland.ac.nz/assets/fmhs/som/psychmed/petrie/docs/2017%20Vax%20Scale.pdf). Article text and PDFs cached under itemtext/.cache/pavic_2022_natural_immunity/.
note: Clean pass with disclosures. (1) SOURCE/MAPPING: mapping_basis=data_labels. The IRW item codes ARE the source column names -- data/pavic_2022_vaccine_conspiracy.py melts the literal list [f'Imm{i}' for i in range(1,4)] out of the PLOS S1 File SPSS deposit (code-derivation pattern 1, core model s3), so no positional slice or renumbering intervenes and Step 5b is exempt. The .sav's own variable labels carry the wording: Imm1 'Natural immunity lasts longer than a vaccination', Imm2 'Natural exposure to viruses and germs gives the safest protection', Imm3 'Being exposed to diseases naturally is safer for the immune system than being exposed through vaccination' (read with pyreadstat; column_names_to_labels). Its value labels carry the anchors, identical for all three items: 1 Completely disagree / 2 Disagree / 3 Neither disagree nor agree / 4 Agree / 5 Completely agree -- the same map the processing script's LIKERT5 dict applies, so the resp axis is label-tied at the source too, not inferred. (2) STEP 3b: instrument confirmed against the paper's Methods -- 'A three-item scale of natural immunity beliefs was taken from the Martin and Petrie [41], Vaccination Attitudes Examination (VAX) scale. Those items were answered on a five-point scale ranging from 1 = completely disagree to 5 = completely agree'. Live data agrees: 3 items, resp 1-5, n=577 per item. The three .sav labels are character-for-character the VAX scale's own published natural-immunity items as printed in Martin & Petrie (2017) Table 2 (Auckland-hosted PDF), differing only in that the deposit drops the terminal full stop on each; the labels are shipped verbatim as read, so no period was added. (3) STORED DIRECTION CHECKED, not assumed: summing the three raw .sav columns gives M=6.60, SD=3.63 over n=577, reproducing the paper's published subscale total (M = 6.60, SD = 3.63) exactly, so the table stores the items raw and in the scored direction (higher = stronger natural-immunity preference). No reverse-keyed items in this subscale. (4) LANGUAGE: administered in Croatian. The paper states 'All the instruments were translated into Croatian, and then back-translated in order to check the validity of the translation.' Neither the article nor its supplements publishes any Croatian wording -- the S1 .sav is the only supplement carrying item text and every label in it is English (zero Croatian item strings; the only Croatian in the file is the derived variable name 'Spol_pismenost_interakcija'). So the translated_substitute fallback applies: the study's own English sits in the base fields, language=Croatian, no _translated columns emitted. translation_source=study_supplied (the deposit's variable labels), which here is also verbatim the instrument publisher's English. (5) STRUCTURE: instructions and section_prompt are NA -- neither the paper nor the deposit publishes any prompt or instruction text for this block, only the 1-5 anchor description already carried by option_text; nothing was invented to fill them. Single trivial section_id; correct_response NA (attitude scale, no key). (6) RIGHTS: no block. The VAX scale is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. Martin & Petrie (2017) 'Understanding the Dimensions of Anti-Vaccination Attitudes: the Vaccination Attitudes Examination (VAX) Scale', Ann Behav Med 51(5):652-660, doi:10.1007/s12160-017-9888-y, prints all 12 items in its Table 2 and carries only a bare copyright line, '# The Society of Behavioral Medicine 2017' -- a notice about the article, not a term governing the instrument (the PANAS case). The authors' own lab hosts the full article PDF openly at https://www.fmhs.auckland.ac.nz/assets/fmhs/som/psychmed/petrie/docs/2017%20Vax%20Scale.pdf (fetched 2026-09-09), and it carries no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause; no rights page for the VAX scale is locatable. Silence is permission, so extracted normally -- nothing quotable to record. The wording additionally sits in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE deposit, though that governs the response data rather than the instrument. (7) A BLOCK WOULD HAVE ACHIEVED LITTLE ANYWAY (irw#2101 shape): the item codes Imm1..Imm3 carry no wording, but the deposit that produced the table is the public PLOS supplement whose variable labels hold the items.
